summary: Implemented search.audit as a fresh explicitly executed file-backed text count scan that returns one typed terminal summary row per invocation without hidden global last-run state.

review.reviewer: separate grill-code review pass (no independent subagent was available)

startingState.worktree: Tracked files were clean before W12-S02 implementation; ignored campaign state had W12-S01 completed and W12-S02 planned, and campaign-state transitions were not included in the scope commit.
startingState.aheadNote: The ahead count includes reachable completed Search scope commits through W12-S01; no upstream changes were present.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning repository's Search production, test, contract documentation and contract-harness files changed, plus this scope's campaign evidence. No sibling repository, package version, publication state or host/SQL engine source was changed.
implementation.auditModel: The public search.audit(root, literal) source creates a fresh inner SearchCountsSource and isolated SourceExecutionContext for each enumeration. SearchExecutionAccounting creates a new scan ID and scope fingerprint per run; SearchAudit copies the immutable terminal summary into one typed 24-column row. Audit predicates remain residual so terminal facts are reported only after the fresh scan completes.
implementation.failureAndCleanup: Inner typed scan failures are represented by one Failed audit row with bounded failure code/path. Writer cancellation remains exceptional, is linked with the execution end-work token, and disposes the linked token source; progress is ended in finally. Ordinary Search sources retain strict failure propagation.
implementation.schemaContract: SearchSchema exposes audit metadata, row-source construction, constructor signatures, primitive-carrier native SearchOutcome enum metadata, all projection fields and matching XML/JSON/Markdown descriptions. The source contract harness now checks scalar and explicit collection fields according to the declared document shape.

scenarios: Fresh repeated and concurrent audit runs have independent scan identities.
Same-root scope profiles have distinct fingerprints and counters.
Empty scans publish one complete exact zero-counter row.
Changed source content is read by the new invocation.
Missing roots publish typed failed audit rows.
Schema, XML, constructor, enum-carrier and compiled SELECT-star contracts align.

iterationDiagnostics: An initial audit/schema-focused run exposed and then corrected expected terminal-reason, enum-carrier and compiler-generated enum-field assertions before the passing verification run.

gateResults.evidence: The exact Release owning-repository suite completed across 21 projects with 1,571 total tests, 1,537 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips; the focused audit/schema set and full Search suite also passed.

The separate review approved fresh per-invocation ownership, failure and cancellation behavior, schema alignment and scope boundaries; exact source hashes and the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are retained.
Fresh repeated/concurrent, profile-isolated, empty-scan, changed-source and missing-root cases pass, and the complete Search semantic suite remains green.
The audit row metadata, compiled SELECT-star result, XML documentation, JSON/Markdown contract and source-contract harness agree; the source harness passes 7 scenarios and 52 assertions.

Fresh inner contexts avoid shared mutable execution state, cancellation links to the writer/end-work boundary, linked resources are disposed, and the Search suite passes concurrent and lifecycle coverage.

knownLimitations: The public audit operation currently covers file-backed text count scans; SearchMany, path-only, byte search and SQL/host terminal-summary transport remain later scopes.
Audit ObservedRows counts rows observed by the underlying count source, while Occurrences counts matcher occurrences; they are intentionally distinct.
The repository suite retained 34 existing classified skips: 31 expected and 3 platform-conditional symlink skips, plus existing package-audit/compiler warnings.
No package was published, pushed, released or installed, and no sibling repository was edited.
